transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, I'm here because I just... I keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. I'm snapping at my team on operations calls, and then I'm doing the same thing to my family at home. And that is just not how I've ever handled things. It's getting out of hand, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to somebody.
Have there been any specific changes, stressors, or events in your life recently that seem to be connected to when these outbursts started happening?

Yeah, there was. It all started about three weeks ago. We had a... well, there was a valve failure at the facility, and it led to an injury on the floor. Ever since that happened, I've just been like this. So, yeah, it's been going on for right around three weeks now.
Since the incident at work, have you noticed that your anger or irritability has been ongoing, even when there isn’t a specific trigger or stressor happening at the moment?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I'm just blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. There doesn't even need to be a real problem happening. I'll be on a normal operations call and just start snapping at my team, or I'll be sitting at home and do the exact same thing to my family. It's just... always there right now, constantly under the surface. And like I said, that is really not how I've ever handled things in the past.
Since this started, have you also been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess so. I don't know if "hopeless" is the right word, but I definitely can't seem to feel good about things anymore. 

Like, my wife will make dinner, or my kids will talk about soccer like normal... and I know I should feel glad to just be sitting there with them. I really should. But it’s like there’s nothing in me that can respond right now. I just can't feel happy about it.
Can you tell me more about the valve failure and the injury? Did you feel personally affected by it, or has it been haunting you in any way since it happened?

Well, yeah, it's definitely been haunting me. I didn't get hurt myself, but I was right there when it happened. 

And now... it just won't leave me alone. I can be sitting at the kitchen table, or just trying to answer some emails from home, and suddenly I'm right back there. I see the flash from the valve failing, I see the smoke filling up the aisle... it just shoves everything else out of my head. It's like I'm watching it happen all over again, and I can't stop it.
Since the incident with the valve failure, have you noticed any physical reactions—like a fast heartbeat, sweating, or shaking—when something reminds you of what happened?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart isn't racing, and I'm not sweating or shaking or anything. It's just the images in my head, but my body feels pretty normal, I guess. I haven't had any physical reactions like you're describing.
Since the valve failure incident, have you had trouble sleeping or staying asleep, especially because of thoughts or images related to what happened?

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty terrible. Most nights I just lie there in bed, and I keep hearing that alarm going off in my head. When I finally do manage to doze off, I end up waking up sweating. I keep having these dreams about all that smoke and people yelling. By the time morning actually comes around, I feel like I never slept at all.
Since the valve failure incident, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened?

No, not really. I mean, I still go into work and do what I need to do. I haven't been staying away from any specific places or people, or changing my routine or anything like that. I'm just going about my normal day... it's just that I have to deal with those images popping up and the exhaustion while I do it. But no, I haven't found myself avoiding anything.
Since the valve failure incident, have you felt more on edge, easily startled, or constantly alert, even in situations that wouldn’t have bothered you before?

Yeah, I definitely have. It seems like any time I hear a forklift beep on the floor, or a compressor kicks on... even if the smoke alarm just chirps at my house, my whole body tightens up. I instantly start looking for exits and trying to figure out what could go wrong next. It's just a constant feeling of being on guard.
Have you noticed that your mood has been consistently irritable or angry, even when you're not thinking about the valve failure incident?

Yeah, I have. Honestly, that's a big part of why I'm here. I just... I keep blowing up at people over nothing. It's like I have zero patience anymore. I've been snapping at people on the operations calls at work, and I'm even doing it at home with my family. It's just not like me at all. That is not how I've ever handled things, but lately, I'm just constantly irritable.
Have you been feeling down or like you're not worth much during most of the day, nearly every day, since this started?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel down or worthless, really. I mean, I'm stressed and exhausted, and obviously dealing with the anger stuff I just mentioned, but... I don't feel depressed or bad about myself. It's more just the constant tension and the flashbacks that are wearing me out.
Since the valve failure incident, have you experienced ongoing feelings of fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame that seem to come from the event itself?

No, not really. I mean, I told you about the anger, but that's more like a short fuse with people, not... not anger about the event itself. And I don't feel guilty or ashamed or horrified. It's just the stress of it all, and the constant feeling like something else is going to blow. But I wouldn't say I have those specific feelings you just listed.
Since the valve failure incident, have you had strong emotional reactions like fear, anger, guilt, or shame specifically when thinking about the event itself?

No, it's... pretty much like what I just said. When I actually think about the valve failing, I don't get hit with a wave of guilt or shame or anything like that. I mean, it's stressful to think about, but I don't suddenly feel terrified or angry at the event itself. The anger is really just me having a short fuse with people right now, not a reaction to the memory.
